verifications.claim: As of April 2, 2026, NASA’s Artemis II mission has launched.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II heads to the moon: Four astronauts... after successfully conducting the translunar injection burn'; R6: 'April 1, 2026 · 3:37 p.m. PT We have liftoff! Artemis II has successfully launched!'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm launch on April 1, 2026, so by April 2 it has launched.

verifications.claim: As of April 2, 2026, NASA’s Artemis II mission is currently orbiting Earth.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'successfully conducting the translunar injection burn... set the spacecraft on the free-return trajectory'; R3: 'human beings have left Earth orbit'; R6: 'Translunar injection burn complete... sending the crew toward the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: By April 2, post-TLI, the mission has left Earth orbit and is en route to the Moon.

verifications.claim: NASA’s Artemis II mission has a four-person crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Four astronauts on the Artemis II mission'; R2: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, as well as Jeremy Hansen'; R3: 'four astronauts'; etc.
verifications.reasoning: All sources explicitly state a four-person crew.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is preparing to travel around the Moon on a 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'journey around the moon after successfully conducting the translunar injection burn... 10 days'; R2: 'orbit the Moon on a 10-day mission'; R6: '10-day mission around the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm the 10-day mission around the Moon; post-launch context shows they are actively en route, aligning with 'preparing to travel' in early phases.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the first human trip to the lunar vicinity in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first time astronauts return to the vicinity of the moon in more than 50 years'; R2: 'first time since 1972'; R3: 'first time in more than 50 years'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated across sources as first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 in 1972.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will splash down in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown'; R4: 'splashdown homecoming into the Pacific'; R6: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'

verifications.claim: The Artemis II spacecraft will perform a fly-around of the Moon before returning to Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'journey around the moon... free-return trajectory'; R3: 'fly around the Moon'; R6: 'around the Moon... lunar flyby'
verifications.reasoning: Described as free-return trajectory slingshotting around the Moon's far side.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II spacecraft will reach distances farther than any human has gone before.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'could travel farther from Earth than any human ever has, breaking the Apollo program’s distance record... surpass the Apollo 13 distance record'; R3: 'likely farther than any human has gone before'; R6: 'broken a distance record... surpassing the record... set by Apollo 13'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly states it will surpass Apollo 13 record.

verifications.claim: Astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Jeremy Hansen are on board Artemis II.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Commander Reid Wiseman... Victor Glover... Christina Koch... Jeremy Hansen'; identical in all sources.
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew names confirmed in every reference.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will spend about 10 days in space to test the Orion capsule’s life support systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'living, sleeping, eating... in it alongside three other people for 10 days... life-support systems'; R2: '10-day mission... verify modern human capabilities'; R6: '10-day mission... test Orion’s systems... life-support'
verifications.reasoning: 10-day duration explicit; testing life support directly mentioned or implied as key objective.

verifications.claim: Artemis II prepares for Artemis III.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R2: 'pave the way for long-term exploration'; R3: 'pave the way for the next human footsteps on the Moon'; R4: 'leadoff in NASA's push toward a landing'; R6: 'paving the way for the Artemis III mission'
verifications.reasoning: Sources state Artemis II tests systems for future missions including III, but phrasing is broader than direct 'prepares for Artemis III'.

verifications.claim: Artemis III plans to land astronauts on the moon in 2028.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'aiming for both to happen in 2028'; R4: 'moon landing near the lunar south pole in 2028'; R6: 'land people on the Moon in 2028'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state Artemis III lunar landing planned for 2028.
